newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai corporate bond yields up, turnover lower.
newsitem.headline: Thai corporate bond yields up, turnover lower.

text.p: Thailand's corporate bond yields edged up, and trading turnover was lower this week as tight money supply and high short-term interest rates hindered institutional investors' demand for bonds, dealers said.
Average daily turnover on the Thai Bond Dealers' Club, the nation's only organised secondary market, was 601.73 million baht compared with 863.94 million baht the previous week.
The average market yield rose to 11.37 from 11.08 last week, club data showed.
"There was continuing correction of yields on most bonds this week. The tight liquidity and high overnight interbank rate also sidelined most institutional investors," one dealer said.

United Communication Industry Plc, among the most active issues in the secondary market, closed at an average yield of 11.25 percent on turnover of 563 million baht for the week. The bond closed at an average yield of 10.91 percent last week.
Finance One Plc closed at an 11.35-percent average yield against 10.9 percent a week ago.
